---
title: "Quickstart"
---

This page shows you how to read the composite from Python. You open one tile
through its [STAC](https://stacspec.org/) item and read a small window of
temperatures. Then you check how many observations support each pixel.

Each tile is an item in a
[Portolan catalog](https://data.source.coop/nlebovits/landsat-lst/catalog.json)
that [Source Cooperative](https://source.coop/nlebovits/landsat-lst) hosts. To
look at the data before you write code, open the
[web map](https://sensable-heat.vercel.app/).

### Before you begin

Install [pystac](https://pystac.readthedocs.io/),
[rasterio](https://rasterio.readthedocs.io/), and [NumPy](https://numpy.org/):

```bash
python -m pip install pystac rasterio numpy
```

The examples read public files over HTTPS. You need no account and no
credentials.

{{< include /_readme/storage-and-access.md >}}

### Hide pixels with few observations

Each item also carries a `qa_count` asset. It holds 12 bands, one for each
calendar month from January through December. Each band counts the
observations of a pixel that passed quality masking in that month. The asset
has no nodata value. A zero means that no observation from that month passed.

The composite withholds a value from any pixel with fewer than five valid
observations across 2021–2025. Near that minimum, one unusual scene can shift
the P95 value. The [methods page](/about/methods.qmd) describes the rule.

The code below reads `qa_count` for the same window as the preceding example. It
sums the 12 bands into a total for each pixel. Then it hides every temperature
that fewer than 20 observations support.

```python
import numpy as np
import pystac
import rasterio
from rasterio.windows import from_bounds

item = pystac.Item.from_file(
    "https://data.source.coop/nlebovits/landsat-lst/"
    "lst-p95-2021-2025/S30W065/S30W065.json"
)
bounds = (-64, -34, -63.9, -33.9)

with rasterio.open(item.assets["lst_p95"].get_absolute_href()) as src:
    window = from_bounds(*bounds, src.transform)
    lst = src.read(1, window=window, masked=True)
    lst_celsius = lst * src.scales[0] + src.offsets[0]

with rasterio.open(item.assets["qa_count"].get_absolute_href()) as src:
    window = from_bounds(*bounds, src.transform)
    # One band per calendar month, January through December.
    monthly_counts = src.read(window=window)

# Valid observations per pixel across all five years.
total_counts = monthly_counts.sum(axis=0)

MIN_OBSERVATIONS = 20
reliable_lst = np.ma.masked_where(total_counts < MIN_OBSERVATIONS, lst_celsius)
print(f"Hidden: {reliable_lst.mask.sum()} of {reliable_lst.size} pixels")
```

`reliable_lst` is a NumPy
[masked array](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/maskedarray.html). It
hides the pixels that the COG marks as nodata and the pixels below your
threshold. Both COGs in an item share one grid. The same bounds select the
same pixels from each.

This window lies in the Argentine Pampas. Every pixel in it has more than 300
valid observations, and the threshold hides none of them. Try a window over a
persistently cloudy region to see the mask take effect. The
[known issues](/about/known-issues.qmd) page describes where cloud cover and
ASTER gaps limit the record.

Choose a threshold that matches how much noise your decision can tolerate, and
report it with your results.
